theme: Hospitality labour and cost data: BLS QCEW/CES leisure and hospitality, hotel wages, cleaning-service prices, STR operating cost datasets
queries_run: gh search repos "leisure and hospitality employment"
gh search repos "restaurant labor cost" "hospitality employment data" "cleaning service price index"
gh search repos "employment cost index accommodation food services" --sort updated
WebFetch on individual repo READMEs / GitHub pages for the candidates below

candidates.name: cori.data.qcew
candidates.what_it_holds: R package (Community Opportunity and Resilience Index project) wrapping the BLS QCEW API/S3 mirror. get_sector_employment()/get_sector_wages() pull county- (~3,100 counties) and state-level employment and average pay for 11 BLS supersectors including 'Leisure and Hospitality' (NAICS 71-72), 1990-present. Snapshots are tagged with a vintage label (e.g. vintage_2025) with a _LATEST pointer on S3 -- i.e. genuinely point-in-time/vintaged QCEW data, not just a live pull. MIT-licensed, 26 commits, last touched within recent weeks.
candidates.why_useful: Direct match to the theme (BLS QCEW leisure & hospitality) and, unusually, ships vintage tags rather than only current-vintage data -- relevant to CONTEXT.md gap #4 (point-in-time macro vintages). Could give county-level hotel/restaurant wage and headcount trends for STR-heavy metros (feeds a hospitality labor-cost proxy for ABNB host/competitor cost pressure, and a leisure/hospitality employment series as a demand-side leading indicator).
candidates.size_hint: package + S3-hosted vintage data (not committed as flat files in the repo)

candidates.name: eighty6-restaurant-labor-reproduction
candidates.what_it_holds: Reproduction package for restaurant wage-share research papers. Pulls BLS QCEW API data (via eighty6data.com) for restaurants (NAICS 7225), full-service (722511), limited-service (722513/722514/722515), and private all-industry wage bills, 2014Q1-2024Q1 (2014-2025 with a paid Pro plan), covering 2,538 US counties plus national and top-100 CBSA aggregates. Ships offline fixtures for 8 sample counties, expected/headlines.json with canonical numbers+tolerances for validation, and a rebuilt minimum-wage history (from Vaghul-Zipperer v1.4.0 + DOL sources). MIT-licensed.
candidates.why_useful: A ready-made, academically-anchored restaurant/food-service labor-cost series (wages, minimum-wage history) at county and CBSA granularity -- a direct proxy for hospitality-adjacent labor cost inflation that could feed an Airbnb host cost / margin-pressure narrative, and the minimum-wage history file is a useful standalone dataset.
candidates.time_coverage: 2014Q1-2024Q1 (free), extendable to 2025 with paid API key
candidates.size_hint: small repo (fixtures + JSON), full data requires live API pull, some tiers paid

candidates.name: alt-nfp
candidates.what_it_holds: Bayesian state-space nowcasting system for US nonfarm payrolls combining CES survey prints, QCEW administrative anchors, private payroll-provider microdata, and cyclical indicators, with 'strict as-of censoring' so backtests only see what was knowable on the day (true real-time/ALFRED-style vintage reconstruction). Pipeline stages: lookups -> download -> ingest -> vintages; model layer in JAX/NumPyro; data persisted to S3-compatible storage with local fallback. MIT-licensed.
candidates.why_useful: A working point-in-time vintage-reconstruction pipeline for BLS employment series (CES+QCEW) -- directly on-point for CONTEXT.md gap #4 (ALFRED-style macro vintages) and gap #17 (nowcasting methods/mixed-frequency). Could be adapted to isolate the leisure & hospitality CES/QCEW sub-series as a vintage-correct labor-cost/employment input.
candidates.geography: US, national (industry detail depends on config)
candidates.time_coverage: not stated explicitly; built for real-time vintage backtesting
candidates.size_hint: codebase + pipeline, no flat data files committed

candidates.name: nfp-nowcast
candidates.what_it_holds: Six-model ensemble US nonfarm payrolls nowcast, described as 'true-vintage backtested' with a QCEW revision estimate component. Full README/data-file detail could not be fetched (page returned a summary card only), so contents beyond the description are unconfirmed.
candidates.why_useful: Another QCEW-vintage-aware nowcasting method (gap #4/#17); worth a closer look if the labour theme needs a template for reconstructing point-in-time BLS employment vintages, but unverified beyond the repo description.
candidates.size_hint: unknown, could not confirm data files

candidates.name: where-has-the-money-gone-U.S-Industry-Pay (AEDR)
candidates.what_it_holds: Long-run BLS QCEW analysis, 1990-2025, 2-digit NAICS sectors nationally, part of an 'American Economic Data Repository' (AEDR) series. Analytical Parquet datasets are hosted on Kaggle (pulled programmatically by the notebook, not committed to the git repo). Findings flag 'Accommodation & Food Services' as one of the sectors with the largest employment-share vs wage-share divergence, though the sector isn't broken out into its own file.
candidates.why_useful: Long national QCEW time series (35 years) with a Kaggle-hosted Parquet mirror; the accommodation & food services divergence finding is a relevant labor-cost/margin signal, though the raw sector cut would need to be re-derived from the underlying QCEW data rather than taken pre-cut from this repo.

candidates.name: NFP_Treemap
candidates.what_it_holds: Self-contained single-file HTML tool built on the BLS API v2 (CES) rendering a drill-down treemap of nonfarm payroll employment by Census NAICS definitions, with anomaly scoring.
candidates.why_useful: A quick way to isolate and visualize the CES leisure & hospitality supersector and its NAICS sub-industries (e.g. accommodation, food services) month by month; more a browsing tool than a dataset, but a fast BLS API v2 client pattern.
candidates.time_coverage: current BLS API v2 series, historical depth per BLS API limits
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: overlaps our existing ~40-series FRED CPI/CES pull, but adds an interactive NAICS drill-down view

candidates.name: south-florida-economic-report
candidates.what_it_holds: Streamlit + Plotly dashboard for Palm Beach, Broward, and Miami-Dade counties combining BLS QCEW, FRED, and IRS SOI data. MIT-licensed. A near-identical fork exists for Michigan's Upper Peninsula (joshuaingber/upper-peninsula-economic-report).
candidates.why_useful: South Florida is a tourism/STR-relevant metro; a reusable QCEW+FRED dashboard template could be repointed at other Inside-Airbnb panel markets (Austin, New Orleans) to pull county-level leisure & hospitality wage/employment series quickly.
candidates.geography: 3 South Florida counties (fork covers Michigan Upper Peninsula, 15 counties)
candidates.size_hint: dashboard app, no large static files

candidates.name: austin-area-labor-market-analysis
candidates.what_it_holds: Excel-based labor market and wage analysis of Bastrop and Caldwell Counties, Texas (Austin metro fringe) using BLS QCEW data for Q4 2024-Q4 2025, covering employment growth, industry contributions, and wage dynamics.
candidates.why_useful: Austin is one of our 13 Inside Airbnb panel cities; county-adjacent QCEW wage/employment detail for the metro could support a local labor-cost cross-check, though the file is Excel-based and industry breakout (whether leisure/hospitality specifically) is unconfirmed.

candidates.name: interstate-wage-gaps
candidates.what_it_holds: Analysis of US state and county wage gaps 2004-2024 using BLS QCEW data, framed around industry-driven churn reshaping regional wage rankings (aggregate geographic inequality stable, but industry composition shifted).
candidates.why_useful: 20-year state/county QCEW wage panel; if it retains industry-level cuts, could isolate leisure/hospitality wage growth by state as a regional labor-cost input, but the industry breakout depth is unconfirmed from the description alone.

candidates.name: Employment-Allocation-Toolbox
candidates.what_it_holds: QCEW employment data ingestion and allocation tool (description-level only; could not confirm README detail or committed data within budget).
candidates.why_useful: Potential generic QCEW ingestion utility; would need direct inspection to confirm it does anything beyond raw employment counts (no confirmed hospitality/wage angle).

notes: gh search repos for the theme's more specific asks -- 'cleaning service price index/dataset', 'STR operating cost dataset', 'hotel wages data' as literal phrases, and 'employment cost index accommodation food services' -- returned zero or irrelevant/noise results (one query, 'bls qcew', spuriously matched an unrelated Google-Cloud-Shell-transcript repo, discarded). No GitHub repo was found that stores a dedicated cleaning-service price index, a housekeeping/turnover-cost dataset, or an STR-specific operating-cost panel (fee schedules, cleaning fee benchmarks, etc.) -- this looks like a genuine gap on GitHub, not just a search-term problem, since QCEW/CES searches surfaced dozens of adjacent labor-market repos but none targeting STR/cleaning cost specifically. The productive vein instead was student/independent QCEW analyses (mostly small, single-purpose, many with no committed data, generated in the last few weeks by what looks like a wave of similar 'BLS QCEW county/metro dashboard' projects) plus two genuinely useful QCEW *tooling* repos: cori.data.qcew (vintage-tagged supersector employment/wages including Leisure & Hospitality, 1990-present) and the alt-nfp/nfp-nowcast pair (true point-in-time BLS employment vintage reconstruction, relevant to the point-in-time rule generally, not just this theme). Web search budget for this session was exhausted (200/200) after 3 queries, so the WebSearch fallback path could not be used to cross-check the cleaning-cost / STR-operating-cost gap further -- a follow-up scout with a fresh search budget should retry 'cleaning fee dataset STR', 'AirDNA operating cost', 'housekeeping turnover cost Airbnb' and similar phrasing. Also worth flagging to the coordinator: hitting the shared WebSearch budget cap mid-run suggests other concurrent scouts are consuming it fast; theme-176 got 3 of ~none remaining.
